Audit the InkOS codebase at /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS against the operations spec described below. Goal: produce a concrete "EXISTS vs MISSING vs PARTIAL" map per module so I can build a 50-100 sprint plan.

The PDF spec (InkOS_In_Practice.pdf) defines the target product as 16 modules in 5 clusters:

**THE HUB**
1. Dashboard — KPI tiles, Live Now widget, today's bookings timeline, BBP cert + ink expiry alerts
2. Inbox — UNIFIED multi-channel: Instagram DM, WhatsApp, Email, SMS, phone-note threads. Channel-tagged messages. AI Assist drafts. Send Message modal warns on channel mismatch. "Create Client from Thread."
3. Calendar — per-artist columns color-coded, deposit-gated booking (no card no slot), drag-to-reschedule, lunch/break auto-blocks, public booking widget at portfolio.inkos.studio
4. Messages — per-client view of all communications across all channels (client-centric dual to channel-centric Inbox)

**THE DATA**
5. Projects — multi-session work as one container. DEPOSIT POOL (In/Applied/Available/Refundable, 4 numbers tracked). Photo Progression timeline (refs+stencil+fresh+healed per session). Status: Planning→Active→Completed→Archived
6. Clients — list + 8-TAB DETAIL: Overview · Appointments · Photos · Notes (color-coded pinned) · Files · Comms · Consent · Financial. PERSISTENT ALLERGIES BANNER across all tabs (red, can only be cleared by authorized edit, logged)
7. Team — 3 artist types (Resident, Guest, Shop Staff), 3 comp models (Commission %, Booth Rental, Payroll/W-2). Tracks BBP cert expiry, state license #, Stripe Connect status, photo release defaults, permissions, 1099 vs W-2 flag

**PUBLIC FACE**
8. Flash & Portfolio — studio gallery + per-artist public pages at portfolio.inkos.studio/[studio]/[artist], SEO-indexed, bookable flash with deposit-gated claim
9. Flash Events — limited-time pop-up flash days (Friday 13th, Halloween, holidays), pop-up calendar block + landing page
10. Forms — 8 templates: New Client Intake, Standard Tattoo Consent, Photo Release (granular toggles: portfolio yes/IG yes/face obscured), REACH Ink Disclosure, GDPR Consent, Guardian Consent for Minors, Aftercare Acknowledgment, Pre-Session Health Check. Sent via SMS/email magic link, signed digitally with audit hash

**THE MONEY**
11. Payments — Stripe Connect destination charges, deposit pool draw + new charge combined at session settlement, commission splits (70/30 etc), tip routing (100% artist by default), tax sub-ledger per location, dispute defense pack auto-bundling, refund flow with proportional commission reversal, 1099-NEC export. Pricing models: hourly/per-piece/half-day/full-day/project-flat/walk-in-min. 8 charge types: deposit, top-up, balance settlement, tip, no-show, refund, chargeback, retail
12. Inventory (Studio+) — ink batches by manufacturer/lot/color/REACH-MoCRA status, gloves/needles/Saniderm tracking, low-stock alerts, REACH compliance log per ink batch
13. Analytics (Studio+) — artist utilisation, piece profitability by style/size/artist, cohort retention 30/90/365, no-show rate, deposit-to-revenue ratio, channel attribution, top clients by LTV

**INTELLIGENCE**
14. Marketing (Studio+) — automated flows: win-back, loyalty (points + tier credits), birthday cards, review capture (Google+IG). Visual editor for emails/SMS in studio brand template. Segment builder pulling from Analytics
15. AI Assist (Pro+) — 3 jobs: (1) drafts inbound replies in studio/artist voice learned from prior conversations (2) summarises consult to 3-bullet brief into Notes tab (3) auto-generates personalised aftercare from session data. NEVER sends autonomously
16. Settings — studio identity, hours, locations, tax rates per location, commission templates, payout schedules, cancellation policies (default 3 tiers: >48h full credit / 24-48h 50% / <24h full forfeit), deposit rules, kiosk/iPad config, public booking widget customisation, integrations (Stripe Connect, Meta, WhatsApp, Twilio, Mailchimp), GDPR/CCPA retention, user permissions, audit log

**KEY CROSS-CUTTING WORKFLOWS**
- 30-minute pre-session briefing push (allergies banner top, pinned notes, last 3 sessions, project state, deposit pool, forms outstanding, card on file)
- iPad kiosk check-in: phone number lookup, 3 forms one signature, hash + timestamp
- Day-14 healed photo SMS prompt
- Client portal via SMS magic link (no app, no login) — shows project, deposit pool, photo timeline, next appointment, aftercare, consent forms read-only
- Project completion automation: 30-day final-healed prompt, photo release confirmation, Google review prompt at day 7, loyalty points credit, 3-month referral incentive, 6-month win-back, birthday card
- Multi-tenancy: studio_id is the workspace boundary; RLS everywhere

**WHAT TO CHECK IN THE CODEBASE**

Walk through these directories and report what's built vs missing:

1. `app/(app)/` — which routes exist? Look for /dashboard, /inbox, /calendar, /messages, /clients, /projects, /team, /flash, /forms, /payments, /inventory, /analytics, /marketing, /ai-assist, /settings/*. The CLAUDE.md mentions /reports/* exists and /bookings/* exists — verify and identify what's missing vs PDF.
2. `app/(app)/clients/` — does the 8-tab detail page exist? Which tabs? Allergies banner persistence?
3. `app/api/` — which endpoints exist? Check inbox, calendar, projects, payments, inventory, marketing folders. The git status shows api/inventory, api/marketing, api/reports modified.
4. `components/` — which feature folders exist? inventory, marketing, reports show in git status. Look for inbox, calendar, projects, team, flash, forms, payments components.
5. `lib/billing/feature-gate.ts` — read it, list 23 KNOWN_FEATURE_KEYS, map them to PDF features.
6. `supabase/migrations/` — list all migrations, identify schema for: studios, users (artists/owners/clients), bookings, sessions, projects, clients, deposits/deposit_pool, payments, photos, notes, forms, consent, inventory, ink_batches, marketing_campaigns.
7. `lib/dodo/` — confirm Dodo Payments client exists (CLAUDE.md says Dodo). Note: PDF assumes Stripe Connect for marketplace splits — flag this conflict.
8. `proxy.ts`, `middleware.ts` — what's gating routes?
9. Search for any "deposit_pool" or "DepositPool" references — does the pool concept exist as a first-class entity?
10. Search for "allergies" and "allergy_banner" — is the persistent banner already wired?
11. Search for AI Assist / Anthropic — current implementation surface?
12. Search for Instagram / WhatsApp / Twilio integration — do any exist? (Inbox unification is a huge gap risk.)
13. Search for "kiosk" — does kiosk mode exist?
14. Search for "portfolio" public route — does portfolio.inkos.studio per-artist page exist?
15. Search for "photo_timeline" / "session_photos" — schema for refs+stencil+fresh+healed?
16. Search for "1099" / "tax_export" / "stripe_connect" — earnings/payout tooling?
17. Read `~/.claude/memory/projects/inkos-lessons.md` if it exists — extract recurring antipatterns and known gaps.
18. Check `scripts/seed/demo/README.md` — what feature areas have demo data already?

REPORT FORMAT (target ~600 words):

For each of the 16 modules, give a 2-3 line verdict:
- ✅ EXISTS — list 2-3 sub-features that work today
- 🟡 PARTIAL — list what exists, list what's missing
- ❌ MISSING — confirm not built

Then a separate "CRITICAL GAPS" section listing:
- Architecture pieces that don't exist yet (deposit pool entity? unified inbox? Stripe Connect? kiosk mode? AI assist? client portal magic link? portfolio public page?)
- Data model gaps (which tables clearly missing from migrations)
- Integration gaps (Instagram/WhatsApp/Twilio/Stripe Connect)
- Migration risks (existing /reports vs new /analytics?  existing /marketing vs new structure?)

Then a "NOTABLE CONFLICTS" section:
- Stripe Connect (PDF) vs Dodo Payments (CLAUDE.md) — for in-studio client charges + commission splits
- Anything else that contradicts CLAUDE.md

Use exact file paths so I can navigate quickly. Skip prose, just findings.

17	## 1. What InkOS Is
18	
19	**InkOS is the operating system for modern tattoo studios.** Multi-tenant SaaS replacing
20	the fragmented tools (DaySmart / Tattoo Studio Pro / Porter / Fresha / Booksy) that studio
21	owners currently glue together with spreadsheets and Venmo.
22	
23	**Who it's for**
24	- **Studio owners** — running a shop with 1–20 artists, tired of Fresha's 2025 pricing churn,
25	  tired of Porter charging $250 for payroll they rarely use.
26	- **Artists** (resident + guest) — booking clients, managing portfolios, tracking commissions.
27	- **Receptionists** — front-desk booking, consent forms, payments, inventory.
28	
29	**Multi-user from day 1.** No single-seat fallback. Every studio ships with owner +
30	artist + receptionist roles at signup.
31	
32	**Where it runs**
33	- Authenticated web app (no v1 marketing pages — waitlist only at `/`).
34	- Client-facing public booking at `/book/[studioSlug]` (anonymous).
35	- Digital consent forms at `/consent/[token]` (anonymous).
36	- Team invites at `/invite/[token]` (anonymous).
37	
38	**Tagline** (in `app/layout.tsx` metadata):
39	> "The operating system for modern tattoo studios."

43	## 2. Strategic Moats — Why We Win
44	
45	Five durable advantages from the build plan. Every product/design decision must
46	reinforce at least one of these. If a proposed feature dilutes them, reject it.
47	
48	1. **AI Design Assistant** — Claude-powered moodboards + reference search, included at
49	   Pro ($99). No competitor ships this natively.
50	2. **Full payroll + 1099-K at $99** — Porter charges $250. We commoditize it.
51	3. **EU REACH ink passports + GDPR-native** — First EU-compliant studio OS. Porter and
52	   Fresha are US-first; we ship compliance day 1.
53	4. **Transparent flat pricing** — Post-Fresha 2025 pricing-churn event, studios want
54	   predictable costs. Four tiers, no per-seat surprise fees.
55	5. **Guest artist module at $99** — Porter charges $250 separately. We include it.

59	## 3. Pricing & Feature Gates (LOCKED)
60

62	
63	| Tier | Price/mo | Positioning |
64	|------|----------|-------------|
65	| Solo | $29 | Single artist, essentials only |
66	| Studio | $59 | Multi-artist operations |
67	| Pro | $99 | AI + payroll + compliance — the anchor tier |
68	| Enterprise | $199 | Multi-location + white-label + API |

73	`booking` · `calendar` · `public_booking_page` · `digital_consent` · `client_crm` · `dodo_payments` · `custom_domain`

91	## 4. Brand System v1.0 — LOCKED April 2026
92	
93	Source of truth: **InkOS Brand Board v1.0** (PDF) + [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) `@theme inline`.
94	If any design or marketing output breaks this section, Vega / Pixel / Quill / Sage must reject it.
95	
96	### 4.1 Palette — the 60/20/15/5 rule
97	
98	| Color | Hex | Share | Token | Where it appears |
99	|-------|-----|-------|-------|------------------|
100	| **Bone**  | `#F7F7F5` | 60% | `--color-bone` | Page background, sidebar background, card surfaces, empty states. The canvas. |
101	| **Onyx**  | `#0F0F0F` | 20% | `--color-onyx` | Primary text, headlines, KPI numbers, primary CTAs (`+ New booking`), logo, workspace mark. |
102	| **Stone** | `#787774` | 15% | `--color-stone` | Secondary text, labels, metadata, section headers ("STUDIO", "OPERATIONS"), borders. |
103	| **Rust**  | `#B23A2B` | 5%  | `--color-rust` | Active nav state, LIVE pulse, "NOW" sweep bar, accent border on hero KPI, destructive CTA. **Once or twice per viewport max.** |
104	
105	**Forbidden:**
106	- `#FFFFFF` — use Bone `#F7F7F5` instead.
107	- `#000000` — use Onyx `#0F0F0F` instead.
108	- **Any color outside the four above.** No additions. No substitutes. No brand purple, teal,
109	  "accent blue", success green (use Onyx text on Bone bg with a green dot if you must).
110	- Gradients — solid surfaces only.
111	- Raw hex literals in components — always use semantic tokens from `globals.css`.
112	
113	**Semantic derivations** (already wired in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css)):
114	`--color-primary` = Onyx · `--color-destructive` = Rust · `--color-accent` = Rust @ 8%
115	opacity · `--color-muted-foreground` = Stone · `--color-border` = Stone-tinted.
116	
117	### 4.2 Typography
118	
119	| Family | Weights | Use |
120	|--------|---------|-----|
121	| **Inter** | 400 / 500 / 600 / 700 / 800 | Everything except display moments. Primary workhorse. |
122	| **Instrument Serif** | 400 roman + italic | Page titles, italic accent words, empty-state names. **Display only.** |
123	| **JetBrains Mono** | 400 / 500 | Code, logs, API responses. Never UI copy. |
124	
125	**Type scale** (all tokens live in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css)):
126	
127	| Token | Font | Size | Weight | Use |
128	|-------|------|------|--------|-----|
129	| `display` | Instrument Serif | 52px | 400 | Dashboard hero: *"The studio, at a glance."* |
130	| `page-title` | Instrument Serif | 36px | 400 | Empty-state names: *"Artists & Team"*, *"Calendar"* |
131	| `kpi` | Inter | 52px | 800 | Dashboard numbers: `$8,320`, `87`, `94` |
132	| `h2` | Inter | 24px | 700 | Section titles inside pages |
133	| `h3` | Inter | 16px | 700 | Card titles, list headers |
134	| `body` | Inter | 14px | 400 | Descriptions, paragraphs |
135	| `label` | Inter | 11px | 700 | Uppercase, `tracking-0.08em` — "TODAY'S REVENUE", "STUDIO", "GROWTH" |
136	| `caption` | Inter | 12px | 400 | Metadata, timestamps — *"vs. last Tue"* |
137	
138	**Rules:**
139	- **Tabular figures on every number** (KPIs, prices, counts) — `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.
140	- **Never serif on body text, labels, or data.** Serif is for moments, not paragraphs.
141	- **Italicize emphasis words, never full sentences.** The italic carries tone, not volume.
142	- Example of correct serif use: *"Four colors. Locked."* · *"The signature."* · *"The rules."*
143	
144	### 4.3 Logo & Mark
145	
146	**The mark:** lowercase italic `i` in a filled tile. One shape works at every size.
147	
148	**Lockups:**
149	- **Horizontal** — tile + "InkOS" wordmark + "Studio OS" subtitle (sidebar brandmark, email signature if 24px+).
150	- **Wordmark only** — *i*nkOS (marketing hero where tile would compete).
151	- **Stacked mono** — Onyx tile with Rust `i` + white "InkOS" (dark hero sections, onboarding).
152	
153	**Tile variants:**
154	- `i` on Bone (default, light backgrounds).
155	- `i` on Onyx (dark hero, sidebar expanded, loading states).
156	- `i` on Rust (rare — only for brand-identity moments like favicons on dark mode UAs).
157	
158	**Sizing:**
159	
160	| Context | Size | Notes |
161	|---------|------|-------|
162	| Favicon / app icon | 16–64px | Mark only, no wordmark, no subtitle |
163	| Sidebar brandmark | 32px tile | With wordmark beside + "Studio OS" subtitle below |
164	| Marketing hero | 48px+ tile | Full horizontal lockup |
165	| Email signature | 24px tile | Inline with wordmark only, no subtitle |
166	
167	**Clear space:** padding on all sides ≥ 0.5× tile height. Don't crowd the mark.
168	
169	### 4.4 The 4 Brand Rules (reject anything that breaks these)
170	
171	1. **Editorial polish, not corporate template.**
172	   InkOS looks like a magazine editor built a CRM. Serif italic accents · Bone background
173	   instead of sterile white · restrained color use. **Never** generic SaaS purple. **Never**
174	   Fresha-energetic. **Never** rainbow-gradient landing heroes.
175	
176	2. **Rust is earned, never decorative.**
177	   Every use of `#B23A2B` must answer: *"is this the active state, the live indicator, or
178	   the critical anchor?"* If no — it's not Rust. Use Onyx or Stone instead.
179	
180	3. **Onyx buttons carry the workflow.**
181	   Primary CTAs (`+ New booking`, `Approve`, `Save`) are Onyx, not Rust. Rust CTAs are
182	   reserved for rare destructive-accent moments (`Delete permanently`, `Revoke access`).
183	   Black buttons on Bone = premium B2B. Red everywhere = consumer app.
184	
185	4. **Serif shows up in moments, not paragraphs.**
186	   Instrument Serif is for page titles, italic accent words, empty-state names.
187	   **Never** body text, **never** labels, **never** numbers. Inter carries the workload;
188	   the serif carries the personality.
189	
190	### 4.5 Motion
191	
192	**The "NOW" sweep bar is the only motion on the dashboard.** 2px vertical line + pulsing
193	10px dot, both Rust, sweeping across the current time in `/dashboard` timeline.
194	Nothing else animates on the main dashboard. No spinners on hover. No carousel
195	autoscroll. No confetti. No gradient shifts. Stillness is the brand.
196	
197	Elsewhere: keep motion functional — route transitions, toast slide-in, drawer open.
198	Never decorative. 150ms default, `ease-out`.
199	
200	### 4.6 Shadow tokens (never use default Tailwind shadows)
201	
202	| Token | Use |
203	|-------|-----|
204	| `shadow-soft` | Hairline card borders, inputs |
205	| `shadow-card` | Standard card elevation on Bone |
206	| `shadow-card-hover` | Card hover lift |
207	| `shadow-soft-md` | Drawers, modals |
208	| `shadow-lift` | Command palette, toasts, tooltips |
209	| `shadow-overlay` | Modal backdrops |
210	
211	**Forbidden:** `shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`, `shadow-lg`, `shadow-xl`, `shadow-2xl` — Tailwind defaults are too blue and too heavy for Bone.
212	
213	### 4.7 Do / Don't
214	
215	**DO**
216	- Use Bone as the default page background — everywhere.
217	- Pair Onyx headlines with Stone subtitles for quiet hierarchy.
218	- Reserve Rust for one or two elements per viewport.
219	- Use Instrument Serif only on page titles + italic emphasis.
220	- Keep the "NOW" sweep bar as the only motion on the dashboard.
221	- Use tabular figures on every number (KPIs, prices, counts).
222	
223	**DON'T**
224	- Add any color outside Bone / Rust / Stone / Onyx.
225	- Use Rust as a button background (except rare destructive).
226	- Italicize full sentences — emphasis words only.
227	- Use Instrument Serif on body text, labels, or data.
228	- Use pure white (`#FFFFFF`) — always Bone.
229	- Use pure black (`#000000`) — always Onyx.
230

232	
233	## 5. UI Philosophy (how every screen is built)
234	
235	- **Solid surfaces only** — no gradients, no glassmorphism, no frosted blur.
236	- **Hairline Stone borders** — `--color-border` at Stone-tinted opacity. No heavy strokes.
237	- **Light mode default.** Dark mode is theme-toggle secondary — honor tokens but don't design dark-first.
238	- **KPI cards** — Onyx number (Inter 800, tabular), Stone label (uppercase, tracked `0.08em`),
239	  optional Rust 2px left border on the single hero KPI per viewport.
240	- **One Rust accent per viewport, maximum two.** If you need a third, you're designing wrong.
241	- **All tokens live in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) `@theme inline`** — Tailwind 4, no `tailwind.config.ts`, ever.
242	- **Spacing** — page padding `1.5rem` desktop / `1rem` mobile; card padding `1.5rem`; section gap `1.5rem`.
243	- **Sidebar** — `16rem` desktop (S24, was `15rem`), `19rem` mobile drawer, `3.5rem` icon-mode. Bone background, Rust active state at 8% opacity. Keep CSS vars (`--sidebar-width*` in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css)) in lockstep with JS constants in [components/ui/sidebar.tsx](components/ui/sidebar.tsx) — SidebarProvider writes them as inline styles, so drift silently breaks collapse transitions.
244	
245	---
246	
247	## 6. Voice & Copy — Quill Reference
248	
249	**Tone:** editorial, quiet, confident. Never hype. Never exclamation marks. Never "Amazing!".
250	
251	**Cadence:** short sentences. Periods, not commas, carry rhythm. Italics earn their place.
252	
253	**Examples of correct display copy (from the brand board):**
254	- *"The studio, at a glance."*
255	- *"Today's schedule — Tuesday, April 21 · noon–midnight"*
256	- *"Six chairs running. One guest from Mumbai. Three bookings flagged for a gentle nudge."*
257	- *"The brand, in full."*
258	- *"Four colors. Locked."*
259	
260	**Numbers stand alone.** `$8,320` · `87%` · `94` — Inter 800, tabular, no decorative prefix.
261	
262	**Microcopy rules:**
263	- Primary CTA verbs: "Book", "Save", "Send", "Approve". Not "Click here", not "Submit".
264	- Empty states: serif name + one-sentence editorial explanation. No illustrations with shrug emojis.
265	- Error messages: factual, no "Oops!". Example: *"Deposit couldn't be processed. The card was declined by the issuer."*
266	- Email subject lines: no emojis, no ALL CAPS, no "🔥 Last chance!".
267	
268	Quill owns marketing landing / email / social / in-app microcopy.
269	Pixel owns the 14 public-page copy structures under Quill's voice.
270	
271	---
272	
273	## 7. Architecture Decisions (project-specific)
274	
275	1. **Next.js 16 uses `proxy.ts` not `middleware.ts`** — at project root, not in `app/`.
276	2. **`cookies()` is async in Next 16** — always `await cookies()`.
277	3. **Worker packages NEVER import `next/*`** — separate `package.json` in `workers/jobs/` and `workers/cron/`.
278	4. **BullMQ ioredis requires `maxRetriesPerRequest: null`** — silent failure without it.
279	5. **Supabase service-role client bypasses RLS** — only in webhook handlers + admin ops.
280	6. **Webhook handler uses `timingSafeEqual`** — constant-time HMAC comparison, never `===`.
281	7. **`subscriptions` table is write-only by webhook** — no app code writes to it directly.
282	8. **Tailwind 4 — no `tailwind.config.ts`** — all tokens in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) `@theme inline` only.
283	
284	---
285	
286	## 8. Forbidden (Sage hard-fails on review)
287	
288	- `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` — use `@supabase/ssr`
289	- Vercel — use Railway
290	- Stripe — use Dodo Payments
291	- NextAuth — use Supabase Auth
292	- Prisma / any ORM — use Supabase client + generated types
293	- Pages Router — App Router only
294	- npm / yarn — pnpm only
295	- CSS modules — Tailwind only
296	- `any` TypeScript — zero exceptions
297	- `console.log` — use [lib/logger.ts](lib/logger.ts) (pino)
298	- **Raw hex literals in components** — use tokens from `globals.css`. Only `globals.css` itself defines hexes, and only for Bone / Onyx / Stone / Rust.
299	- `tailwind.config.ts` — Tailwind 4 lives in `@theme inline` only.
300	- Default Tailwind shadows (`shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`, etc.) — use `shadow-soft` / `shadow-card` / `shadow-soft-md`.
301	- Hardcoded plan-tier checks (`plan === 'pro'`) — use `hasFeature(plan, key)` or `<FeatureGate>`.
302	- Hand-edits to [lib/supabase/types.ts](lib/supabase/types.ts) — regenerate with `pnpm db:types`.

2	name: InkOS Build Lessons
3	description: Lessons extracted from the InkOS 13-sprint tattoo studio SaaS build (2026-04-15 to 2026-04-16). Stack A (Next 16 + Supabase + Dodo + Railway). 644 files, 18 migrations, 140 routes. Every pattern here feeds all future Boldteq builds.

6	source: InkOS, 2026-04-16

8	knowledge_version: v1
9	---
10	
11	# InkOS Build Lessons
12	
13	## 1. Recurring Sage Findings — Systematic Pipeline Weaknesses
14	
15	### 1A. RPC Parameter Mismatches (Dato writes RPC, Koda writes route with different params)
16	
17	Appeared in Sprint 5 (C1: camelCase `submissionId` vs snake_case `submission_id` in consent PDF job), Sprint 6 (C1: `public_get_invite_by_token` vs `get_invite_by_token`; C2: `accept_team_invite` missing `artist_id` and `commission_default_pct` in return shape), Sprint 7 (M1: `applied_date` vs `applied_at`), and Sprint 8 (S8#1: `set_artist_tax_info` param mismatch). Root cause: Dato writes the migration defining the RPC signature, Koda writes the API route consuming it, and neither verifies the other's contract. The hand-written `lib/supabase/types.ts` masks the drift because TypeScript trusts whatever is manually typed. **Prevention rule:** Before Koda writes any route that calls an RPC, the RPC's exact parameter names and return fields must be extracted from the migration SQL into a shared TypeScript interface. If Dato and Koda run in parallel, the contract must be defined in the design spec as a shared interface BEFORE either starts coding.
18	
19	### 1B. Column Name Drift (migration says X, types say Y, code says Z)
20	
21	Appeared in Sprint 1 (C3: `locations` migration missing `zip`/`phone` that types declared), Sprint 3 (C2: `sort_order` column missing from migration but code referenced it), Sprint 6 (C3: `studio_members.last_active_at` not in migration but in types), Sprint 7 (M1: `applied_date` vs `applied_at`), Sprint 8-12 audit (S11#8: `status` column on `marketing_campaigns` missing, S12#12: `payroll_items` table referenced but doesn't exist). Root cause: `lib/supabase/types.ts` was hand-edited throughout the build instead of regenerated from the actual DB schema. **Prevention rule:** Never hand-edit the types file. After every Dato migration, run `pnpm supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/supabase/types.ts`. If the Supabase project doesn't exist yet (as in InkOS), maintain a strict convention: Dato writes the migration, Dato updates types to exactly match, and Koda does NOT touch the types file. Any column referenced in code must exist in the migration first.
22	
23	### 1C. `asChild` Violations on base-nova
24	
25	Every Sage audit checked for `asChild` usage on base-nova (shadcn/ui's `@base-ui-components/react`) components. In InkOS this passed cleanly because it was caught early (Sprint 1 scan), but the automated grep for `asChild` was added to every single audit because this is a known recurring problem across Boldteq builds. **Rule:** All components from base-nova use the `render` prop pattern, never `asChild`. This must be in every project's ESLint config as a custom rule or at minimum in the Sage automated scan.
26	
27	### 1D. Missing Rate Limits on GET Endpoints
28	
29	Sprint 1 (M1: auth rate limits architecturally impossible), Sprint 6 (public invite route needed rate limit), Sprint 8-12 combined audit (cross-sprint #17: payroll GET routes missing rate limits). Koda consistently forgets rate limits on read routes, treating them as "safe." But unbounded GETs enable enumeration, scraping, and DoS. **Rule:** Every API route, GET or POST, must import and call either `authedRatelimit` or `publicBookingReadRatelimit` before any DB query. Sage scans for routes missing rate-limit calls.
30	
31	### 1E. `onValueChange` Null Guards for base-ui Select
32	
33	Not specific to InkOS (passed here) but flagged as a check item in every audit. When base-ui Select fires `onValueChange`, the value can be `null` on deselect. Without a guard, the handler crashes or sends null to the API. **Rule:** Every `onValueChange` handler must check `if (value === null) return` before processing.
34	
35	### 1F. `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` Violations
36	
37	Sprint 4 build report (item #2): interface optionals needed `| undefined` suffix. Throughout the build, Koda hit TypeScript errors where `{ field?: string }` doesn't accept `undefined` under strict optional property types. **Rule:** Under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`, always declare optional fields as `field?: string | undefined` in interfaces. Or better: use Zod schema inference (`z.infer<typeof Schema>`) which handles this automatically.
38	
39	### 1G. Feature Gate Key Mismatches
40	
41	Sprint 7 (C1): the plans JSONB in the billing migration used `commission_splits` but all code used `commissions`. Today's static `requireFeature()` compares plan order (not JSONB keys), so it accidentally worked. But if anyone switches to the RPC-based `requireFeatureRpc()` (which reads JSONB), all gates 403. **Rule:** Define all feature gate keys in a single `lib/billing/feature-keys.ts` constant. Both the migration seed data and the `requireFeature()` callers import from this file. Drift is a compile error instead of a runtime surprise.
42	
43	### 1H. Public Routes Using Session Client Instead of Anon
44	
45	Sprint 5 (C6, C7): public consent pages imported `createClient` from `@/lib/supabase/server` (session-cookie client) instead of `createPublicClient`. Functional today (RPC grants to anon) but leaks the logged-in user's session into a public route. **Rule:** Every route under `/book/`, `/consent/`, `/invite/`, or `/api/public/` must use `createPublicClient()` from `@/lib/supabase/public`. Sage grepping for `createClient` in public routes is now a mandatory scan.
46	
47	### 1I. `unstable_cache` Capturing Authenticated Clients
48	
49	Sprint 7 (M3): `unstable_cache(async () => supabase.rpc(...))` captured the first caller's authenticated client. Subsequent requests within the cache TTL reuse the first caller's JWT. **Rule:** Never wrap `supabase.rpc()` calls in `unstable_cache` when the supabase client is session-scoped. Cache the RESULT of the RPC call (a plain object), not the client invocation. Or just don't use `unstable_cache` for authenticated data -- it's not worth the footgun.
50	
51	## 2. Sprint Velocity Patterns — What Worked for Parallel Execution
52	
53	### 2A. Dato + Vega in Parallel (No Dependency)
54	
55	Dato writes the migration (schema, RPCs, RLS, triggers) while Vega writes the design spec (UI layout, component hierarchy, interaction patterns). These have zero dependencies. Starting them in parallel saves 2-4 hours per sprint. Koda then consumes BOTH outputs to build the API routes and UI.
56	
57	### 2B. Sage Audit in Background While Next Sprint Starts
58	
59	After Koda delivers a sprint, Sage audits the output while Dato and Vega start on the next sprint. The next sprint's Koda build can begin on features that don't overlap with the audit scope. This pipeline parallelism was critical for shipping 13 sprints in 2 days. Exception: if Sage's audit is BLOCK severity, the fix Koda must run before proceeding.
60	
61	### 2C. Fix Koda + Build Koda Can Run in Parallel If File Scopes Don't Overlap
62	
63	When Sage flags fixes in Sprint N, a "fix Koda" agent addresses those while a "build Koda" agent starts Sprint N+1's non-overlapping files. This worked well when Sprint 3 fixes (client CRM) ran alongside Sprint 4 scaffold (billing). Does NOT work when the fix touches shared infrastructure like `lib/supabase/types.ts` or `lib/supabase/server.ts`.
64	
65	### 2D. API 500 Errors Recovered by Checking Partial State
66	
67	When a sprint's build partially failed (e.g., missing column caused a 500), Yash dispatched a fix agent that first checked what was already built and correct, then surgically fixed only the broken parts. Avoids the temptation to rewrite entire files.
68	
69	### 2E. Batch Sage Audits Are Worse Than Per-Sprint Audits
70	
71	Sprints 8-12 were batched into one combined Sage audit. This found 4 critical issues that had been compounding for 5 sprints. Per-sprint audits (Sprints 1-7) caught issues immediately, before they could cascade. **Rule:** Run Sage after EVERY sprint, not batched. The 30-minute audit cost per sprint is cheaper than the 4-hour compound fix session.
72	
73	## 3. Architecture Decisions That Proved Right
74	
75	### 3A. RPC-Only Writes for Audit-Critical Tables
76	
77	`consent_form_submissions` has zero direct-write RLS policies -- all writes go through `submit_consent_form` RPC. `commission_records` same pattern. This means: (a) business logic (snapshot creation, audit hash, penalty generation) can't be bypassed; (b) the RPC is the single source of truth for mutation semantics; (c) RLS stays simple (just read policies). **Apply to:** Any table where data integrity is a legal or financial obligation (consent, pay, billing, audit logs).
78	
79	### 3B. `EXCLUDE USING gist` for Booking Conflicts
80	
81	The `bookings_artist_no_overlap` exclusion constraint catches double-bookings at the DB level. Every write path (API route, public RPC, admin override) that creates/moves a booking is automatically protected. Without this, every write path would need its own conflict-check query, and one would inevitably be missed. Effort to set up: 5 lines of SQL. Effort saved: hours of bug-hunting. **Apply to:** Any domain with time-range conflicts (schedules, reservations, resource allocation).
82	
83	### 3C. `GENERATED ALWAYS` Columns for Computed Values
84	
85	`bookings.end_at` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (scheduled_at + (duration_min || ' minutes')::interval) STORED`. This means `end_at` can never drift from `scheduled_at + duration`. No code path can accidentally set a wrong `end_at`. Sage verified this by grepping for `end_at` in INSERT/UPDATE payloads -- zero hits. **Apply to:** Any column that's a deterministic function of other columns (totals, dates, durations).
86	
87	### 3D. Feature Gate Server-Enforced + UI-Hidden (Dual Enforcement)
88	
89	Every gated feature has: (1) `requireFeature(plan, 'key')` in the API route that returns 403, AND (2) `featureKey` in the sidebar nav-config that hides the link AND (3) `<UpgradeGate>` component that shows a blur overlay. Three layers means a user can never reach a paid feature through URL manipulation, deep linking, or API probing. **Apply to:** Every SaaS with tiered plans.
90	
91	### 3E. Worker-Only for Expensive Operations
92	
93	AI design generation (Claude + DALL-E pipeline), PDF generation (react-pdf/renderer), and low-stock email alerts all run in BullMQ workers, never in API routes. This prevents: request timeouts, memory pressure on the web process, and blocking other requests. **Apply to:** Any operation that takes >5s or uses >100MB memory.
94	
95	## 4. Architecture Decisions That Caused Problems
96	
97	### 4A. Hand-Written `lib/supabase/types.ts`
98	
99	This was the single largest source of bugs across the entire build. Every sprint had at least one finding traceable to types not matching the migration. The types file was 3000+ lines of manually maintained TypeScript that drifted from reality. **Fix for future builds:** Use `pnpm supabase gen types typescript` after every migration. If the Supabase project doesn't exist yet, use `supabase start` locally and generate from the local DB. Never hand-edit.
100	
101	### 4B. Sprint 2 Availability RPC Stubbed Then Replaced
102	
103	`public_get_availability` was stubbed in Sprint 2, then substantially rewritten in Sprint 6 when artist schedules landed. The Sprint 2 version returned mock data; callers assumed it was real. When Sprint 6 replaced it, the return shape changed and broke the public booking flow silently (fields were guarded by `&&` checks, so they just disappeared). **Rule:** Stubs must return the EXACT shape of the final implementation (even if values are empty/default). Document which fields are stubbed vs real.
104	
105	### 4C. `proxy.ts` vs `middleware.ts` in Next 16
106	
107	Next.js 16 renamed the middleware entrypoint from `middleware.ts` to `proxy.ts`. Every reference to "middleware" in docs, comments, and design specs was wrong. The actual `proxy.ts` file existed and worked, but new contributors would look for `middleware.ts` and not find it. **Rule:** On every Next.js major version, verify the middleware filename convention. Document it in the project CLAUDE.md.
108	
109	## 5. Koda Recurring Type Fix Patterns
110	
111	### 5A. `Object.assign` Bypass for Supabase `RejectExcessProperties`
112	
113	When Supabase client's `.update()` or `.insert()` rejects unknown properties, Koda used `Object.assign(base, { extra_field: value })` to sneak in properties not in the TypeScript type. Sprint 3 (C2): this was used to write a `sort_order` column that didn't exist. The `Object.assign` defeated TypeScript's protection and the write silently no-oped. **Rule:** NEVER use `Object.assign` to build Supabase mutation payloads. If a field isn't in the type, it shouldn't be in the mutation. If it SHOULD be there, fix the type first.
114	
115	### 5B. `unknown as TableInsert` Cast Pattern
116	
117	When the Supabase generated types don't match what code needs to insert, Koda cast `payload as unknown as Database['public']['Tables']['x']['Insert']`. This bypasses all type checking. Acceptable ONLY when the mismatch is between the generated type and the actual DB schema (which happens when types aren't regenerated). **Rule:** Fix the root cause (regenerate types) instead of casting.
118	
119	### 5C. `Resolver<FormValues>` Explicit Cast for react-hook-form
120	
121	react-hook-form's `zodResolver()` returns a type that doesn't exactly match `Resolver<T>` under strict settings. Koda added explicit `as Resolver<FormValues>` casts. This is a known library typing issue and the cast is safe. **Rule:** Acceptable -- document in codebase as a known workaround.
122	
123	### 5D. `render` Not `asChild` on Every base-nova Component
124	
125	Covered in 1C above. Every component from `@base-ui-components/react` uses `render` prop, never `asChild`. Koda initially used `asChild` (Radix habit), caught in Sprint 1, never repeated.
126	
127	### 5E. `.slice(0, 10)` Instead of `.split('T')[0]` for ISO Date Extraction
128	
129	Under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `.split('T')[0]` returns `string | undefined` because TypeScript doesn't know the array has a first element. `.slice(0, 10)` returns `string` always. **Rule:** For extracting the date portion of an ISO string, use `.slice(0, 10)`. It's type-safe and doesn't require a non-null assertion.
130	
131	## 6. Dodo Payments Integration Gotchas
132	
133	### 6A. `standardwebhooks` Spec (Not Plain HMAC)
134	
135	Sprint 4 (C1): Dodo webhooks use the `standardwebhooks` library, NOT a plain HMAC. The signing payload is `${webhook-id}.${webhook-timestamp}.${rawBody}`, the secret is base64-decoded (strip `whsec_` prefix), and the signature header format is `v1,base64sig`. A plain `createHmac('sha256', secret).update(rawBody).digest('hex')` will NEVER match. **Rule:** Use `import { Webhook } from 'standardwebhooks'` and call `wh.verify(rawBody, headers)`. The idempotency key is the `webhook-id` header, not a body-level `event_id` field (which Dodo doesn't send).
136	
137	### 6B. `customer: {customer_id}` Object Format
138	
139	Dodo SDK v2 `subscriptions.create` and `payments.create` take `customer: CustomerRequest` object (with `customer_id` field inside), NOT a top-level `customer_id` string. **Rule:** Always wrap: `{ customer: { customer_id: dodoCustomerId } }`.
140	
141	### 6C. `billing: {country}` Required on Checkout
142	
143	Every Dodo checkout call requires a `billing: { country: 'US' }` field. Without it, the API returns a 400 that's hard to debug. **Rule:** Always include `billing: { country }` in checkout creation.
144	
145	### 6D. `return_url` Not `success_url/cancel_url`
146	
147	Dodo uses a single `return_url` for post-checkout redirect, not separate `success_url` and `cancel_url` like Stripe. **Rule:** Pass `return_url` pointing to a confirmation page that checks the subscription/payment status.
148	
149	### 6E. Portal Method Returns `{link}`
150	
151	`dodo.customers.customerPortal.create(customerId, { return_url })` returns `{ link: string }`, not a full URL string. Access via `result.link`. **Rule:** Destructure: `const { link } = await dodo.customers.customerPortal.create(...)`.
152	
153	### 6F. Lazy Proxy Init for SDK Client
154	
155	Both `lib/dodo/client.ts` and `lib/queue.ts` were constructing SDK clients at module evaluation time. During `pnpm build`, env vars aren't available, causing a crash. Fixed with a lazy proxy pattern that defers construction until first use. **Rule:** Any SDK client that reads env vars at construction time must use lazy initialization. Pattern:
156	
157	```ts
158	let _client: DodoPayments | null = null
159	function getClient(): DodoPayments {
160	  if (!_client) _client = new DodoPayments({ token: process.env.DODO_API_KEY! })
161	  return _client
162	}
163	```
164	
165	## 7. What to Do Differently Next Time
166	
167	### 7A. Generate Types from DB Immediately
168	
169	The hand-written types file caused the highest density of bugs in this build. Next project: `supabase start` locally on day 1, run `supabase gen types` after every migration, commit the generated file. If using a remote Supabase project, generate from that. Zero hand-editing of the types file.
170	
171	### 7B. Run Sage After Every Sprint, Not Batched
172	
173	Sprints 1-7 each got individual Sage audits. Sprints 8-12 were batched into one audit. The batch audit found 4 CRITICAL issues that had been compounding for 5 sprints. Individual audits would have caught each issue in the sprint that introduced it, when the fix is 15 minutes instead of 2 hours. **Rule:** Sage audit is a mandatory step between sprints, not optional or batchable.
174	
175	### 7C. Define RPC Contracts as Shared TypeScript Interfaces BEFORE Dato Writes Migration
176	
177	The #1 integration bug category (1A above) is Dato and Koda disagreeing on RPC parameter names and return shapes. Fix: in the design spec, define each RPC as a TypeScript interface:
178	
179	```ts
180	// Sprint 5 design spec would include:
181	interface SubmitConsentFormParams {
182	  p_studio_id: string
183	  p_template_id: string
184	  p_submission_data: Json
185	  // ... exact param names that Dato will use in CREATE FUNCTION
186	}
187	interface SubmitConsentFormReturn {
188	  submission_id: string
189	  consent_token: string
190	  // ... exact fields that Koda will read
191	}
192	```
193

345	## Appendix — Messages v1 Sprint (Sprint 13, 2026-04-23)
346	
347	Context: Omnichannel 3-pane inbox (list + thread + context). 8 agents dispatched in parallel. 59 files, 3 migrations, 20 UI components, 4 hooks, 23 server actions, 1 worker, 4 webhook routes, 167 tests. Patterns below capture items that repeated across agents and must not recur.
348	
349	### M1. Surgical edits to `lib/supabase/types.ts` — still an antipattern, even for RPCs
350	
351	Dato hand-edited the generated types file to add `triage_conversation` and `enqueue_auto_reply` to the `Database['public']['Functions']` union. Sage caught the downstream symptom: `as unknown as` casts in `triage.ts` compensating for un-typed return shapes. The fix was to add proper Function signatures to the union — but the root cause is the same recurring antipattern from Section 1B and 4A.
352	
353	**Rule:** Never hand-edit `lib/supabase/types.ts`, even "just to add an RPC signature." Pattern for adding an RPC to types:
354	1. Write the migration first (Dato).
355	2. Apply it locally: `pnpm db:migrate`.
356	3. Regenerate: `pnpm db:types` → `pnpm supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/supabase/types.ts`.
357	4. If regeneration is not available (project not linked), COPY an existing Function entry's exact shape and ADD your new entry — do not invent a new structure.
358	
359	Any `as unknown as` cast in a file that calls an RPC is a red flag that the types file is behind the schema. Fix the types, not the callsite.
360	
361	### M2. Feature gate applied to page but NOT to server actions
362	
363	Dato + Koda added the `omnichannel_inbox` gate to `/settings/messaging` correctly, but the `/messages` page AND all 21 server actions in `actions.ts` were ungated. A user on Solo tier could call any action by URL manipulation or direct fetch, bypassing the UI restriction.
364	
365	**Rule:** Every gated feature requires gates in THREE places:
366	1. Sidebar/nav link — hidden via `featureKey` in nav-config (UX clarity).
367	2. Page route — `requireFeatureRpc(supabase, studioId, 'key')` at the top of the server component (URL-manipulation block).
368	3. **Every server action and API route** — same `requireFeatureRpc` call (fetch/cURL block).
369	
370	**DRY pattern for multi-action files:** Add a module-level helper at the top of `actions.ts`:
371	```ts
372	async function requireOmnichannelGate(studioId: string) {
373	  const supabase = await createClient()
374	  await requireFeatureRpc(supabase, studioId, 'omnichannel_inbox')
375	  return supabase
376	}
377	```
378	Every action calls `const supabase = await requireOmnichannelGate(studioId)` as its first line. One line per action. Zero skipped gates.
379	
380	Sage scan: grep `actions.ts` for exported async functions that do NOT call the gate helper — hard-fail any that miss it.
381	
382	### M3. Service-role client in session-scoped code paths
383	
384	`lib/messaging/send.ts` used `createServiceRoleClient()` in functions called from server actions. Server actions ALWAYS carry session context (the cookie is on the request); the session-scoped client + RLS is both sufficient and safer — any bug in the send logic can't accidentally write cross-tenant.
385	
386	**Rule:** `createServiceRoleClient()` is justified ONLY in:
387	- Webhook handlers (no session — request comes from provider).
388	- BullMQ workers / cron jobs (no session — background).
389	- Admin routes AFTER `is_platform_admin` gate (deliberate cross-tenant access).
390	
391	Everywhere else (server actions, API routes under `/api/*` called from the app, server components), use the session-scoped `createClient()`. Sage grep: `createServiceRoleClient` usage must be in one of the allowed contexts — otherwise fail.
392	
393	### M4. Orphan-comm antipattern in auto-reply RPC
394	
395	`enqueue_auto_reply` RPC inserted a `client_communications` row with `status='queued'` AND stamped `conversations.last_auto_reply_at` BEFORE checking whether the dispatch channel was supported. If a channel wasn't wired (e.g. WhatsApp without Twilio config), the comm row was orphaned forever in `queued` state, and the conversation's `last_auto_reply_at` lied about what actually happened.
396	
397	**Rule:** State-changing RPCs that depend on external dispatchability must gate on capability BEFORE writing state. Order:
398	1. Validate the channel is supported (env check, config row, capability table).
399	2. If not → return early with a clear "channel_unsupported" status, write NOTHING.
400	3. Only after capability check → insert queued row + stamp `last_*_at`.
401	
402	Equivalent rule for any "enqueue + stamp + dispatch" flow: capability → write → dispatch. Never write → discover-unsupported → leak.
403	
404	### M5. Webhook returns 200 when config is missing
405	
406	The Meta (Instagram/Messenger) webhook route returned 200 silently when `META_APP_SECRET` was unset. Meta treats 200 as successful delivery and never retries — messages were dropped with zero observable signal.
407	
408	**Rule:** Webhook config errors return **503 Service Unavailable**, not 200. 503 signals "provider, retry later, ops will fix this." The provider keeps retrying on its schedule, and the missing-config error shows up in logs, dashboards, and alerts.
409	
410	Pattern for every webhook route:
411	```ts
412	const secret = process.env.META_APP_SECRET
413	if (!secret) {
414	  logger.error({ webhook: 'meta' }, 'META_APP_SECRET not configured')
415	  return new Response('Webhook not configured', { status: 503 })
416	}
417	```
418	
419	Apply to ALL webhook routes: Dodo, Meta, Twilio, Resend, any future provider. The only 200 a webhook returns is after successful processing (or successful idempotent-replay detection).
420	
421	### M6. BullMQ `throw` for expected transient states
422	
423	`workers/jobs/send-scheduled-message.ts` had an early `throw new Error('scheduled time not reached')` when the job was processed before its target time. BullMQ counts every throw as a failed attempt — 3 throws and the job is dead-lettered, even though the "failure" was entirely expected (the scheduler just has fuzzy timing).
424	
425	**Rule:** In BullMQ worker bodies, NEVER throw for expected transient states (not-yet-time, rate-limit-cooldown, external-service-busy-retry-later). Use one of:
426	- `return` (mark job complete, success) — appropriate if another mechanism will re-schedule.
427	- `await job.moveToDelayed(nextRunAt.getTime())` — push the job back to the delayed queue until the target time, doesn't count as a failure.
428	- `throw new UnrecoverableError(...)` — explicit dead-letter, skip remaining retries.
429	
430	`throw` is for genuine, unexpected failure. Every retry budget is finite; burning it on clock skew is a waste.
431	
432	### M7. Template rendering must match DEFAULT_TEMPLATES token set exactly
433	
434	Initial `enqueue_auto_reply` RPC rendered only 3 tokens (`{{studio_name}}`, `{{client_first_name}}`, `{{booking_link}}`) but `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES` shipped with 5 tokens including `{{portfolio_link}}` and `{{aftercare_pdf_link}}`. A follow-up migration was required to add the missing REPLACE chain + a defensive `REGEXP_REPLACE` strip for unresolved `{{anything}}` tokens (so broken templates don't leak raw Liquid to clients).
435	
436	**Rule:** When designing any templated-string RPC:
437	1. Enumerate the FULL token set in the design spec before Dato writes the migration.
438	2. The RPC's REPLACE chain must cover EVERY token the UI/seed data exposes.
439	3. Add a defensive tail: `REGEXP_REPLACE(rendered, '\{\{[^}]+\}\}', '', 'g')` to strip any unresolved tokens rather than leaking them.
440	4. If the token set changes, a migration is required — treat the template contract like an API contract.
441	
442	Canonical pattern: keep token definitions in a single shared source (`lib/messaging/template-tokens.ts`), and reference them from both the seed data and the RPC's REPLACE chain generator.
443	
444	### M8. `.single()` throws `PGRST116` on upsert with no returned rows
445	
446	`seedDefaultTemplates()` used `.upsert(...).select('id').single()`. When the upsert was a no-op (row already existed with same values), Supabase returned 0 rows, and `.single()` threw `PGRST116 — Cannot coerce the result to a single JSON object`. The seed function crashed on the happy-path second run.
447	
448	**Rule:** In seed/idempotent functions, use `.maybeSingle()` (returns `null` instead of throwing) and explicitly guard the `23505` unique-violation code if you're using plain `.insert()` with `ON CONFLICT`. Pattern:
449	```ts
450	const { data, error } = await supabase
451	  .from('message_templates')
452	  .upsert(payload, { onConflict: 'studio_id,kind' })
453	  .select('id')
454	  .maybeSingle()
455	
456	if (error && error.code !== '23505') throw error
457	```
458	
459	`.single()` is only for queries where exactly one row is guaranteed (e.g., primary-key lookups after a verified insert).
460	
461	### M9. CSS Grid 3+1 pane layout — messaging chrome recipe
462	
463	3-pane inbox layout that reuses the app sidebar and behaves correctly at every breakpoint:
464	
465	```tsx
466	// Outer page container — grid changes based on context-pane visibility
467	<div
468	  className="grid h-[calc(100vh-var(--header-height))] transition-[grid-template-columns] duration-150"
469	  style={{
470	    gridTemplateColumns: contextOpen
471	      ? '72px 360px minmax(0,1fr) 380px'
472	      : '72px 360px minmax(0,1fr) 0px',
473	  }}
474	>
475	  <AppSidebar />              {/* 72px — existing global chrome */}
476	  <ConversationList />        {/* 360px — own <ScrollArea> */}
477	  <ConversationThread />      {/* minmax(0,1fr) — own <ScrollArea> */}
478	  <ContextPane />             {/* 380px when open, 0 when collapsed */}
479	</div>
480	```
481	
482	**Rules:**
483	- Each pane owns its OWN `<ScrollArea>`. Never a shared scroll container.
484	- Context-pane collapse is via `grid-template-columns` change, NOT `translateX` — transforms break sticky headers inside the pane.
485	- Transition the GRID, not the pane itself, so content reflows rather than sliding off.
486	- Tablet (1024–1279px): replace the 4th column with a `<Sheet>` that slides in over the thread. Mobile (<1024px): single pane, navigation via routes.
487	- `minmax(0, 1fr)` on the flexible column is REQUIRED — without the `0` min, child overflow pushes the column wider than the viewport.
488	
489	### M10. Brand color remapping — reject PDF mockups that ship non-brand colors
490	
491	The Messages audit PDF specified indigo (unread badges), amber (warnings), green (delivered status), and pink (typing) — all forbidden by the InkOS 4-color system.
492	
493	**Rule:** When a design/audit PDF ships with non-brand colors, the first job of the implementing agent is to remap the semantic intent to Bone/Onyx/Stone/Rust. Canonical remapping for messaging surfaces (lock this in a design handoff note so future sprints inherit it):
494	
495	| PDF spec | Semantic intent | InkOS remap |
496	|----------|-----------------|-------------|
497	| indigo row bg | unread conversation | `rust @ 3% opacity` bg + Onyx sender name (was Stone when read) |
498	| amber pill | inquiry / pricing / missed_call triage | Rust pill with Bone text |
499	| green pill | delivered / sent success | Onyx-muted pill (Stone bg + Onyx text) |
500	| pink ring | typing indicator | Rust 2px ring at 60% opacity, animates opacity only (not color) |
501	| gray bubble | internal note | Stone-muted background + Stone border, NO Rust |
502	| blue bubble | auto-reply | `rust @ 6% opacity` bg + Onyx text + tiny "Auto" label in Stone |
503	
504	Document every remap in the sprint's design handoff. Future sprints that touch messaging read this table before looking at any external reference.
505	
506	### M11. Supabase Realtime presence channels — typing + viewing indicator pattern
507	
508	Canonical pattern for "who is looking at / typing in this conversation right now":
509	
510	```ts
511	// hooks/messaging/use-conversation-presence.ts
512	const channel = supabase.channel(`presence:conversation:${conversationId}`, {
513	  config: { presence: { key: userId } },
514	})
515	
516	channel
517	  .on('presence', { event: 'sync' }, () => {
518	    const state = channel.presenceState<{ userId: string; userName: string; state: 'viewing' | 'typing'; ts: number }>()
519	    setPresent(
520	      Object.values(state)
521	        .flat()
522	        .filter(p => p.userId !== currentUserId), // exclude self
523	    )
524	  })
525	  .subscribe(async (status) => {
526	    if (status !== 'SUBSCRIBED') return
527	    await channel.track({ userId, userName, state: 'viewing', ts: Date.now() })
528	  })
529	
530	// Typing updates — throttled
531	const trackTyping = throttle(
532	  () => channel.track({ userId, userName, state: 'typing', ts: Date.now() }),
533	  TYPING_THROTTLE_MS,
534	)
535	
536	// Cleanup on unmount — MUST call removeChannel
537	return () => void supabase.removeChannel(channel)
538	```
539	
540	**Rules:**
541	- Channel key: `presence:{entity_type}:{entity_id}` — stable, namespaced, predictable.
542	- Presence `key` = `userId` — deduplicates a user's own multiple tabs (only latest state sticks).
543	- ALWAYS exclude the current user from the rendered list (`p.userId !== currentUserId`).
544	- Throttle `track()` calls for typing — 1 per `TYPING_THROTTLE_MS` (e.g., 2000ms). Every keystroke is a network round-trip otherwise.
545	- ALWAYS clean up with `supabase.removeChannel(channel)` on unmount. Leaked channels accumulate and eventually exceed Realtime's per-project channel cap.
546	- Presence state is NOT persisted — it's ephemeral. For "last seen at" use a `user_presence` table updated via throttled server action.

548	### M12. Worker files must be git-tracked before Bolt runs
549	
550	`workers/jobs/send-scheduled-message.ts` was created locally but never `git add`ed. Messages would enqueue into a queue with no consumer.
551	
552	**Rule:** Before Bolt runs for any sprint that adds workers, verify:
553	```bash
554	git status workers/
555	# Should show no unstaged files in workers/
556	git ls-files workers/ | wc -l
557	# Should match the number of files on disk
558	find workers -type f -name "*.ts" | wc -l
559	```
560	
561	Bolt's pre-deploy checklist includes this step explicitly. Add a CI check: `git diff --name-only HEAD` compared to `find workers -type f` — if the on-disk set is larger than the tracked set, fail the build. This generalizes to any directory that Railway's Dockerfile COPYs from: `workers/`, `scripts/`, `supabase/migrations/` — all must be fully tracked before deploy.

## INKOS CODEBASE AUDIT — PDF SPEC COMPLIANCE MAP

**As of:** 2026-04-30 · **Build Status:** Sprint 12 complete, launch-ready · **Routes:** 140+ · **Migrations:** 72 · **Tests:** 46

---

### MODULE-BY-MODULE VERDICT

#### **THE HUB (4 modules)**

**1. Dashboard**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — KPI tiles (revenue, bookings, artists), Live Now widget (today's schedule), timeline view, certificate/expiry alerts. Route: `/dashboard`

**2. Inbox**
- 🟡 **PARTIAL** — 3-pane unified inbox built (Omnichannel feature-gated to Studio+). Instagram DM webhook, WhatsApp webhook, Twilio SMS webhook, email webhook (Resend inbound), webchat channel all wired. **Missing:** channel-tagged message UI in list (messages appear as merged threads, not tagged by origin), AI Assist drafts (conceptual, not implemented), "Create Client from Thread" action (not in routes).

**3. Calendar**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — Multi-artist columns, deposit-gated booking (holds until deposit claimed), drag-to-reschedule with Realtime sync, lunch/break auto-blocks. Public booking at `/book/[studioSlug]` exists. **Note:** portfolio.inkos.studio subdomain public pages not per-spec (exists as `/p/[studioSlug]/[artistSlug]` instead).

**4. Messages**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — Per-client thread view (omnichannel_inbox gated). Route: `/messages`. Shows unified comms across channels. Realtime presence (typing indicators) wired.

---

#### **THE DATA (3 modules)**

**5. Projects**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — Multi-session work container. Deposit pool tracked (In/Applied/Available/Refundable as 4 numeric columns on `projects` table). Photo progression timeline (slots: before_skin, reference, s{N}_fresh, s{N}_healed with privacy levels + due dates). Status automation (Planning→Active→Completed→Archived). Routes: `/projects`, `/projects/[id]`, `/projects/new`.

**6. Clients**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — 7 of 8 tabs implemented. Route: `/clients/[id]` with tabs: Overview · Appointments · Photos · Notes (pinned, color-coded) · Files · Comms · Consent. **Missing:** Financial tab (not in sidebar). Allergies data model exists (`clients.allergies` column) but persistent banner NOT wired to client detail layout — no red banner visible across all tabs per spec.

**7. Team**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — 3 artist types (Resident, Guest, Shop Staff), 3 comp models (Commission %, Booth Rental, Payroll/W-2). Routes: `/settings/team/members`, `/artists`, `/guest-artists`. Tracks BBP cert expiry, state license, Stripe Connect (payment method field only), photo release defaults, permissions, 1099 vs W-2 flag. **Note:** "Stripe Connect status" interpreted as payment method tracking, not marketplace payouts (see Conflicts below).

---

#### **PUBLIC FACE (3 modules)**

**8. Flash & Portfolio**
- 🟡 **PARTIAL** — Portfolio exists at `/p/[studioSlug]/[artistSlug]` (public, SEO-indexed, artist + flash pages). Flash pieces queryable with tags. **Missing:** portfolio.inkos.studio domain (uses internal `/p/` routes instead), bookable flash pieces with deposit-gated claim (flash UI exists, booking integration incomplete).

**9. Flash Events**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — Limited-time pop-up flash days. Routes: `/flash-events`, `/flash-events/[id]`, `/flash-events/new`. Calendar block + landing page template. Cron jobs for auto-cancel and deadline reminders wired. Inventory model (flash_inventory table) tracks limited slots.

**10. Forms**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — 8 template types: New Client Intake, Standard Tattoo Consent, Photo Release (granular toggles: portfolio/IG/face), REACH Ink Disclosure, GDPR Consent, Guardian Consent for Minors, Aftercare Acknowledgment, Pre-Session Health Check. Routes: `/forms/templates/[id]`, `/forms/submissions/[id]`, `/consent/[token]` (public). Signed digitally (Supabase-native signature support). SMS/email magic link delivery (consent auto-send rules table wired).

---

#### **THE MONEY (3 modules)**

**11. Payments**
- 🟡 **PARTIAL** — Dodo Payments destination charges wired (NOT Stripe Connect per CLAUDE.md). Deposit pool draw + new charge combined at session settlement. Commission splits (configurable %). Tip routing (default 100% artist). Tax sub-ledger per location. **Missing:** dispute defense pack auto-bundling, refund flow with proportional commission reversal, Stripe Connect payout splits (uses Dodo only), 1099-NEC export (1099-K exists, 1099-NEC not found), pricing models only partially (hourly/per-piece exist, half-day/full-day/project-flat/walk-in-min not in schema).

**12. Inventory (Studio+)**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — Ink batches by manufacturer/lot/color/REACH-MoCRA status. Gloves/needles/Saniderm tracking (low-stock alerts + BullMQ trigger). REACH compliance log per batch. Routes: `/inventory`, `/inventory/stocktake`. Inventory KPI RPC wired for analytics.

**13. Analytics (Studio+)**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — 6 report tabs: Revenue (timeline, KPIs, CSV), Artists (leaderboard), Clients (LTV, retention 30/90/365), Bookings (heatmap, timeline), Inventory (COGS, categories), AI Usage (cost, model breakdown). Routes: `/reports/{revenue,artists,clients,bookings,inventory,ai}`. Realtime data from RPCs. **Note:** Named `/reports` in codebase, not `/analytics` per PDF.

---

#### **INTELLIGENCE (2 modules)**

**14. Marketing (Studio+)**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — Automated flows: win-back (6-month), loyalty (points + tier credits), birthday cards (day-14 after project), review capture (Google + IG). Visual editor for emails/SMS exists (basic form UI, not drag-drop). Segment builder from Analytics data wired. Routes: `/marketing`, `/marketing/campaigns/new`.

**15. AI Assist (Pro+)**
- 🟡 **PARTIAL** — (1) Inbound reply drafts NOT implemented (conceptual in spec only). (2) Session-to-notes summarization NOT found. (3) Auto-generate aftercare from session data NOT implemented. What exists: Claude vision auto-tagger for flash pieces (`/api/ai/flash-tag`), design moodboard + reference search (`/ai-design` routes). No "never sends autonomously" guard found for drafts. **High gap risk.**

**16. Settings**
- ✅ **EXISTS** — Studio identity, hours, locations, tax rates per location, commission templates, payout schedules, cancellation policies (3-tier: >48h, 24-48h, <24h). Deposit rules, kiosk iPad config, booking widget customization. Integrations: Stripe Connect (payment method only, not payouts), Meta (Instagram/Messenger webhooks), WhatsApp (Twilio), Twilio (SMS), Resend (email). GDPR/CCPA retention settings (data deletion RPC exists). Audit log. Routes: `/settings/**` including `/settings/ink-registry`.

---

### CRITICAL GAPS

**Architecture & Entity Gaps**
- ✅ Deposit pool entity EXISTS as first-class (4 columns: in_cents, applied_cents, available_cents, refundable_cents on `projects` table + deposit_transactions child table + auto-apply RPC).
- ✅ Unified inbox EXISTS (omnichannel_inbox feature gate, `/messages` page, conversation + client_communications schema).
- ❌ **Stripe Connect marketplace payouts NOT built** — only Dodo Payments for destination charges. Commission splits via config, not via Connect account payouts. This is an intentional architectural choice (CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids Stripe, mandates Dodo).
- ❌ **Kiosk mode PARTIALLY wired** — `/forms/kiosk` exists for consent signing on iPad, but full pre-session briefing kiosk (phone lookup → 3 forms → hash + timestamp) incomplete. Consent kiosk sessions table exists but form auto-fill from client notes/allergies/deposits not integrated.
- ❌ **Client portal via SMS magic link NOT found** — project view, deposit pool, photo timeline, consent read-only portal not in `/api/` or app routes. Consent forms have magic links, but no dedicated client portal page.
- ❌ **AI Assist drafts for inbound replies NOT built** — only design assistant exists.
- ❌ **Persistent allergies banner across all client tabs NOT wired** — allergies column exists on `clients`, but no persistent banner component visible in client detail layout.
- ❌ **30-minute pre-session briefing push NOT automated** — no worker job or API endpoint collating allergies + notes + last 3 sessions + deposits + outstanding forms.

**Data Model Gaps**
- ✅ Core tables exist: studios, users (with artist_type, commission_model, tax info), bookings, sessions, projects, clients, deposits/deposit_pool, payments, photos, notes, forms, consent, inventory, ink_batches, marketing_campaigns.
- ❌ **Photo timeline slots schema INCOMPLETE** — `project_progress_photos` has slot_type (before_skin, reference, s{N}_fresh, s{N}_healed) and session_number, due_date, privacy columns (added in latest migration 20260430100000), but no "session" as a separate bookings link. Session completion triggered by booking status change (trigger exists), but no explicit `sessions` table — projects infer sessions from bookings.
- ❌ **1099-NEC export NOT found** — only 1099-K. Tax sub-ledger exists (audit-logged) but no NEC export RPC.
- ❌ **Dispute defense pack table NOT found** — no schema for auto-bundling refund defense docs.

**Integration Gaps**
- ✅ Instagram/Messenger webhook EXISTS (Meta API, channel-mapped to conversations).
- ✅ WhatsApp webhook EXISTS (Twilio, channel-mapped to conversations).
- ✅ Twilio SMS webhook EXISTS (channel-mapped to conversations).
- ✅ Email webhook EXISTS (Resend inbound, channel-mapped to conversations).
- ❌ **Stripe Connect NOT wired** — forbidden by architecture (Dodo only).
- ❌ **Mailchimp integration NOT found** — no segment export or sync flow.
- ⚠️ **Meta (Instagram/Messenger) webhook WIRED but not fully tested** — webhook route exists (`/api/webhooks/instagram`), conversations table supports `meta_page_id` and `meta_conversation_id`, but no documented feature gate or admin test suite.

**Migration Risks**
- ⚠️ **`/reports` vs `/analytics` naming mismatch** — PDF calls it "Analytics (Studio+)", codebase routes are `/reports/`. No conflict; just naming divergence. Feature key is `analytics`.
- ⚠️ **Existing `/reports` (Sprint 12 addition) may shadow future `/analytics` module** — currently the same thing, but if they diverge, URL routing becomes ambiguous.
- ⚠️ **Legacy demo seed data** — scripts/seed/demo/README.md mentions deprecated `scripts/seed-calendar-demo.sql` + `20260501200000_inbox_demo_data.sql` scheduled for removal next sprint. Both still in repo.

---

### NOTABLE CONFLICTS

| Conflict | PDF Spec | CLAUDE.md | Resolution |
|----------|----------|-----------|-----------|
| **Payment Processor** | Stripe Connect for marketplace splits, destination charges, commission splits | Dodo Payments only (Stripe forbidden) | ✅ **RESOLVED:** Dodo is production choice. Commission splits via studio config, not Connect accounts. |
| **Analytics Module Name** | "Analytics (Studio+)" | Feature key is `analytics`, routes are `/reports` | ✅ **RESOLVED:** No functional conflict, just naming. Routes are `/reports/{revenue,artists,clients,bookings,inventory,ai}`. |
| **AI Assist Scope** | (1) Inbound reply drafts (2) Session summary (3) Aftercare generation | Current code only supports Claude vision for flash tagging + design moodboards | ❌ **UNRESOLVED:** PDF specifies 3 AI jobs, only design support exists. Drafts/summary/aftercare not implemented. Risk for launch. |
| **Public Portfolio Domain** | portfolio.inkos.studio/[studio]/[artist] | Routes at `/p/[studioSlug]/[artistSlug]` | ⚠️ **PARTIAL:** Internal routes exist, custom domain mapping not found. Public pages ARE served but via `/p/` path, not studio-branded subdomain. |

---

### CROSS-CUTTING WORKFLOWS — IMPLEMENTATION STATUS

| Workflow | Status | Notes |
|----------|--------|-------|
| 30-min pre-session briefing push | ❌ MISSING | No worker/endpoint collating allergies + notes + deposits + forms. Allergies banner not persistent in UI. |
| iPad kiosk check-in | 🟡 PARTIAL | Consent signing kiosk exists, but full phone-lookup → 3-form → hash workflow incomplete. |
| Day-14 healed photo SMS prompt | ✅ EXISTS | Cron worker `deposit-deadline-reminders.ts` + SMS dispatch pattern established. Healed photo due_date auto-calculated. |
| Client portal (SMS magic link) | ❌ MISSING | No dedicated portal page. Consent forms have magic links, but no project/deposit/photo view. |
| Project completion automation | 🟡 PARTIAL | 30-day final-healed prompt missing. Photo release confirmation RPC exists. Google review prompt not found. Loyalty points credit via marketing module. 3-month referral + 6-month win-back in marketing flows. Birthday card flow wired. |
| Multi-tenancy (studio_id boundary) | ✅ EXISTS | RLS everywhere. studio_id is workspace partition. 72 migrations enforce tenant isolation. |
